conflict_topics: sleep needs for work/exams vs need to wake early for shifts
schedule accommodations (which nights to shift shower/cooking)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, personal reasons (hospital shift, client presentations, exams) which makes positions clear.
Agent C plays a mediating/clarifying role proposing partial solutions; D offers a limited accommodation (cooking at night, Sunday shower change).
There is some repeated restatement of unwillingness by D and repeated appeals by others, which slows resolution but keeps positions clear.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D agreed to shower the night before on Sundays only ('Okay. Just on Sunday nights? I can do that.' — Turn 8). That is an explicit, limited concession: A's Sunday need was accommodated, but B's and C's objections about multiple weekday mornings (the next four weeks) were not accepted, so the main incompatibility over weekday 4:45 showers remains.
position_change_notes: Agent D conceded one specific change: showering on Sunday night instead of Sunday morning ('Okay. Just on Sunday nights? I can do that.' — Turn 8) and moved cooking to nights (Turn 16/28).
Agent A accepted the Sunday-night arrangement (Turn 9) and did not press further.
Agent B continued to request additional nights (Turn 10) and did not get agreement; position unchanged.
Agent C consistently highlighted their direct disturbance and proposed compromises (Turn 13, 15) but did not obtain broader concessions; position unchanged.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: 'Agent D, 4:45 is very early.' — Turn 2: 'I know. My hospital shift starts early for the next four weeks.' (Incompatible needs—D must rise early; others dislike being woken.)

Turn 3: 'I have major client presentations on Mondays. I can't be tired for those.' — Turn 4: 'My exams are on Tuesdays and Thursdays... 4:45 is a problem for me too.' (More household members state stakes, widening the conflict.)

Turn 5: 'My room is right between yours and the kitchen, Agent D. I can hear everything.' — Turn 6: 'What if I cook my lunch the night before?... It would be quieter.' (D offers a partial accommodation reducing cooking noise; shower issue remains.)

Turn 7: 'How about just for Sunday nights, could you shower the night before? That's the one that really impacts my work.' — Turn 8: 'Okay. Just on Sunday nights? I can do that.' (Explicit agreement on Sunday nights — partial settlement.)

Turn 10: '...could you do the same for me on Monday and Wednesday nights? The shower at 4:45 would still wake me up before my exams.' (B introduces an additional accommodation demand beyond the Sunday concession; unresolved.)

Turn 11: 'I can't do that for another two nights. I need the shower in the morning to wake me up properly before my shift.' — Turn 12: 'But you just agreed to do it for Agent A on Sundays. My exams are just as important as his work.' (Direct refusal vs renewed demand; opposing positions remain.)
Turn 13: 'What if you just do it for one of the nights... ?' — Turn 14: 'One night was already a lot for me. I can't do another one.' (Mediator proposal rejected; entrenched disagreement persists.)

Turn 15: 'This isn't just about one or two nights... I'm going to be woken up every single weekday.' — Turn 16: 'I'm already cooking at night to keep it quieter. That's the biggest change I can make.' (Scope of harm expanded by C; D holds to limited changes.)

Turn 17: 'But the shower is still really loud.' — Turn 18: 'I understand that, but... I need the shower to wake up for work. There's nothing else I can change about my mornings.' (Core incompatibility reiterated; no resolution.)

Turn 21: 'I've already told you, I can't change that. I've done what I can with the cooking.' — Turn 22: 'You're showering at night for Agent A. So it's not that you can't.' (C challenges consistency of D's claim, heightening disagreement.)

Turn 23: 'That was for one night. It's not something I can do every day.' — Turn 26: 'It's about being able to do my job. I need the shower in the morning to be alert at the hospital. One night is not the same as every day.' (D reaffirms limits; conflict over weekdays remains.)

Turn 27: 'And I'm the one who's going to be woken up every day. It's not just one night for me, it's four weeks.' — Turn 28: 'And I'm the one getting up at 4:45. I've already changed my cooking routine to help.' (Positions restated; main incompatibility still unresolved.)

substantive_insights: Core tension is practical: D needs a morning shower to be alert for hospital shifts; others need uninterrupted sleep for exams/work—these needs directly conflict during early mornings.
A limited accommodation (moving cooking to night) reduces some noise but does not address the dominant noise source (shower).
A one-night concession (Sunday) was acceptable to D but insufficient for roommates with repeated weekday obligations, creating a persistent unresolved issue.
Attempts to negotiate (B asking for additional nights, C proposing compromise) failed because D frames the morning shower as necessary for job performance and refuses further changes.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 4 because the final status is partially_resolved.
